text:
nora: heads up — after the driver 12.6.3 roll in staging we're seeing a 20-40% p99 latency jump on small-batch (batch<=8, seq<=64) inference. looks like KV prefetch paths are getting misrouted and causing cache thrash :thinking_face:

mike: ugh. timeline? which node pool started the bump?

nora: rolled at 1937998000 across staging-autoscale pool. first alert at ~1938001000 from perf-alerts. ci smoke for runtime perf also flaked on triton-matmul-test (see ci-bot below).

ci-bot: [CI] perf-smoke/runtime-matrix — FAILED — relative latency +32% (golden baseline 58ms -> 76ms) — logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/1938001

jess: copied a short perf trace. looks like prefetch requests are routed to different KV shards for the same session intermittently. flame snippet: `prefetch->dispatch(shard=3)` then next token `get_kv(shard=7)` for same token stream. that's a cache miss pattern. :no_good:

liam: that's… odd. could be router hashing change in cudnn/cuBLAS dispatch? or a Triton kernel selection change picking a different tiled matmul that invalidates prefetch alignment. Did the driver bump coincide with a Triton minor bump?

nora: we did not change Triton. only node images pulled nvidia-driver 550.x -> 12.6.3 (driver pkg name: nvidia-driver-550-12.6.3). PyTorch/Triton pinned to same builds.

sam: can you paste the perf invocation you ran? i'll try to repro locally with a minimal harness.

jess: here's the quick repro command I used on staging with dtrace-enabled run:
```
./run_perf.sh --model rlhf-small --seq 64 --batch 4 --trace kv,prefetch --nvprof /tmp/nvprof.out
```
nvprof snippet shows repeated memcpy + kernel launch pairs where prefetch kernel targets different GPU addresses for same session id; timestamps align with the driver memcpy scheduling changes.

mike: ok, plan: 1) bisect driver 12.6.3 -> 12.6.1 on a small subset, 2) enable extra routing logs in the prefetch router (cheap flag), 3) if repro quick, revert node image. who's owning the bisect? @liam?

liam: i'll take the bisect. starting with image-2026-03-12 (driver 12.6.1) vs image-2026-03-17 (driver 12.6.3). will run reduced cluster with traffic shadow. ETA ~2h.

deploy-bot: Rollout patch image-2026-03-12 -> staging-autoscale initiated by liam at 1938002100 (0/10 nodes drained)

nora: also adding a temporary guard in router: if prefetch target shard != expected_shard then skip prefetch and fall back to synchronous get_kv. that should remove thrash while we bisect. i'll push patch to main -> canary.

jess: put a perf snapshot in GCS: gs://redwood-perf/snapshots/1938001234-kv-misroute.npz (includes nvprof + router logs).

mike: heads-up: potential rollout blocker for releases if this affects hosted customers. open a small incident and tag product/security just in case.

nora: opened incident-2026-03-18-01, linked perf snapshot and CI failure. tagging @product & @security.

liam: bisect results so far: image 2026-03-15 still good, 2026-03-16 shows the shift. narrowing. suspect change is in NVIDIA kernel scheduling within driver 12.6.3 that changed memcpy ordering. running microbench for cudaMemcpyAsync pacing now.

sam: if driver is root cause we can coordinate a rollback for staging quickly, but for prod we'll need safety windows. also let's add a synthetic test to CI that simulates repeated prefetch across shards to catch regressions early.

mike: agreed. add test + guard + revert candidate. if bisect finishes positive, we'll raise rollback PR for node image. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
